title: Explain quality management from trigger to disposition
prompt: Explain how a quality-relevant logistics or production event becomes an inspection, a business decision, a stock consequence, and possible corrective action.
expected_points: business event and inspection lot origin
procurement, production, inventory or sales boundary
follow_up_questions: Why is an inspection result not the same as a usage decision?
Why can accepted material still be unavailable?
red_flags: treats QM as one accept/reject flag
starts with a transaction code instead of inspection trigger
does not separate quality decision from stock state

title: Expected goods-receipt inspection lot is missing
prompt: A supplier goods receipt is posted for a material that should be quality inspected, but no inspection lot is created and the stock is immediately usable. How do you investigate?
expected_points: confirm exact goods-receipt event, material, plant and movement context
check active inspection type and material quality settings
separate inspection-control cause from inventory symptom
prove the fix with a clean receipt event
follow_up_questions: Why is manually creating a lot a weak permanent fix?
What data would you compare with a material where the process works?
red_flags: moves stock to quality inspection without proving trigger logic
does not check inspection origin or material settings

title: Usage decision accepted but stock remains unavailable
prompt: Inspection results are complete and the usage decision is accepted, but production still cannot consume the material. How do you find the broken state transition?
expected_points: check whether the lot is stock relevant
inspect stock posting from the usage decision
reconcile inspection-stock balance and material document
separate ERP quality state from EWM warehouse execution if EWM is used
follow_up_questions: Which system owns the quality decision and which owns physical warehouse execution?
When would a manual stock posting make the incident harder to diagnose?
red_flags: assumes accepted usage decision automatically means unrestricted stock
posts a transfer movement before reconciling quality disposition

title: Trace quality evidence into customer delivery
prompt: A customer requires a quality certificate with a delivery. Trace the quality and sales context needed to produce the correct evidence without weakening the customer requirement.
expected_points: relevant inspection results or batch characteristics
usage-decision or quality status where applicable
sales owns delivery while QM owns quality evidence
follow_up_questions: What would you check if the product is accepted but the certificate is missing?
Why is removing the certificate requirement not a real fix?
red_flags: treats certificate as an unrelated print form
removes customer control to unblock delivery
